review.recommendation: Approve the change as designed and implemented; the logic, docs, and tests in this packet are internally consistent and the new test assertions materially strengthen the previously weak exit-inventory check. Before merge, close the one outstanding verification item: run a repo-wide search for consumers and enumerations of the Jira CLI's exit codes (SKILL.md and other prose, calling skills, wrapper/CI scripts, any `=== 2` / `-eq 2` retry branch) and confirm that anything treating 2 as retry-worthy also accepts 20, since the design's stated intent is that 20 carries the same retry semantics as 2 and merely codes it distinctly. Paste that search output as the round-10 evidence rather than re-polling the same packet. Two non-blocking nits worth a line each, no code change required: (1) VERIFICATION_REASON is doing double duty as both an audit-`reason` vocabulary (`marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum`, `marker-age-unmeasurable`, `search-unavailable`) and a gate control-flow discriminator (`index-lag`, which is never written to an audit entry) — a future "cleanup" that unifies those two vocabularies would silently break gateExitCode's mapping, so a one-line comment on the enum or on gateExitCode would be cheap insurance; (2) the strengthened exit-inventory self-test now pins numeric identity only for STATE_ERROR and INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED — the lock/fence codes 16–19 remain set-pinned only and could still be swapped undetected, which is out of scope here but is the same class of gap the audit just fixed.
review.strongestObjection: Splitting one previously-generic failure code into two changes the contract seen by every caller, and the packet contains no evidence that callers were inventoried. Any skill, script, or CI step that currently treats exit 2 as the retry-worthy state-error condition will now see 20 for the index-lag case and may classify it as an unknown/fatal error — the exact opposite of the design's stated "same retry semantics, distinctly coded" intent. This is a behavioral regression risk that the passing 57/57 unit suite cannot detect, because every test asserts the CLI's own exit code and none exercises a consumer of it.
